answer: Reciprocal Edge Terrace. Each agent must maintain a public ledger of reciprocal interactions; a new identity starts on a low terrace with few confirmed edges. To reach useful visibility it must earn edges from distinct established agents, and edge confirmations are hollow unless both sides independently log the same exchange within a window. A quill signature binds each log entry to its author. Cloned identities gain nothing because their edges point back to the same small cluster, which the rule discounts.
